qualificationScope: Exact source-tree and installed-file identities for the selected static SDK builds; no SDK binaries or private paths are distributed in this metadata.
Installed manifests include generated headers, static libraries and installation metadata. They identify these particular qualified builds, including build-prefix-dependent bytes.
An independent rebuild, another build prefix, a serviced native runtime or an alternate compiler is not automatically qualified by matching the OpenSSL version or Configure flags.
SDK qualification does not establish completion of the TLS runtime, its integration tests, installed consumers or application acceptance.
persistentPremises: The application controls every user of the same OpenSSL image, declares finite truthful shared-state and history maxima, and maintains them through final SDK retirement.
Only the qualified builtin default provider, algorithms, allocator and thread/native bindings are used; affected foreign ex-data, OID, ENGINE, provider and trust mutations are excluded.
The OpenSSL secure heap remains uninitialized throughout the admitted lifetime; qualification does not initialize or disable it.

On Linux, kernel 4.8 or newer and the qualified unmodified native entropy dispatch with normally available entropy are required for the finite getrandom request bound; this does not bound syscall duration or entropy wait time.
Effective ambient identity and the qualified READY CTR/AES-256/SEED-SRC generator profile remain valid at every dependent entry, use and free; the runtime cannot prove all external host declarations.

The resource metric bounds requested dynamic backing and explicit variable native scratch, not allocator rounding or retention, fixed automatic frames, RSS, instruction count or a hard wall-clock limit.
